history.sg_progress: The United Nations Treasury reached out to all field offices and received confirmation of the active bank signatories. It continues to confirm with each of the field offices when the expiration date of the delegation of authority for bank signatories has been reached in order to ensure that the signatories are still active. In addition, the Business Transformation and Accountability Division periodically monitors and informs the United Nations Treasury whenever a bank signatory has been separated or has retired from the Organization; the United Nations Treasury then withdraws the delegation of authority as bank signatory for the respective staff member. The Administration considers this recommendation to have been implemented and requests its closure by the Board.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration update the information on signature authority with the missions to ensure that personnel registered correspond to the operational needs.
history.administration_response: The Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget and the United Nations Treasury have completed the reconciliation of bank signatories for bank accounts and continuously ensure that they are up to date. The Administration wishes to highlight that this will be an ongoing activity, in particular because there will always be a gap between when an action is taken at Headquarters and when the action is taken by the bank, and reiterates its request to the Board to close the recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Tests were carried out and showed a number of discrepancies. Sometimes the signatories listed in the United Nations file did not match those shown on the bank confirmation, or the signatories appearing on the bank confirmation were not included in the United Nations file. Given these continued shortcomings, the Board considers that the update of designated signatories needs to continue for the accounts.

history.sg_progress: The Administration requests the closure of this recommendation by the Board. The United Nations Treasury has completed the reconciliation of bank signatories between the United Nations records, the United Nations offices and the banks. As this is an ongoing exercise, every time there is a change in bank signatories, there will be a time gap between when action is taken by the United Nations Treasury and when the action is confirmed and completed by the bank. Many countries are continuously enhancing their “know your customer” regulations, leading to more requirements when adding bank signatories. This increases the time required to clear the proposed bank signatories and add them to the banks’ records. It is important to note there are several mechanisms at the United Nations that prevent bank signatories from becoming outdated in the system, such as setting the delegation of authority expiration for bank signatories to a maximum of two years, which forces the local office to review the role of each bank signatory. Monitoring the delegation of authority for separated or retired staff triggers the removal of bank signatory authority for such staff and the notification to the banks about the removal. These measures are further enhanced with the just-in-time funding of the United Nations bank accounts, which ensures that there are minimal balances in the United Nations accounts globally that could be subject to fraud.
